chapter: Carnegie Hall, nicknames and later career
title: Hours at the Reno Club and ballroom dance signs
summary: Basie says his hours were 10 till 4, he played foxtrots but the lindy hop came later, and ballrooms had signs for the dance types.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I know : No you don't? All right. Did you play 8 PM to 8 AM?

No. The lindy hop came was later, as far as I was concerned. At the ballrooms at that time, they used to have a sign that said "foxtrot" and it would light up, and they have things like the foxtrot and the patrons would get in 2 would pull a sign that said "waltz," and another sign that said lines ... that's how they did that, "one step."

Whoever was sitting on the end of the bandstand, you know -- they'd pull out the sign that said "foxtrot." they'd be playing waltzes and all of I used to think it was awful silly, because they'd know what a for trot was, and they'd got to know to hear that a waltz is a waltz. they are gonna waltz, they got to waltz, and not foxtrot, just Just the same as like with a piano, putting a sign on a piano and say 'piano'. that says
